- Overestimate prices in the short term after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (sentiment < -0.5) — model reacts too slowly to bearish signals.
- Overreact to positive sentiment (sentiment > 1.0) by over-forecasting, especially in early days of the horizon.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after recent peaks, ignoring downward momentum.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts — model delays correction when sentiment turns negative, especially if recent sentiment was positive.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early periods (first 5–7 days) and underestimate late periods (last 5–7 days), especially when sentiment is volatile.
- When sentiment is mixed or trending sideways, model tends to average out, leading to underperformance in volatile periods.
